newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 15.

text.p: One Mexican crude shipping port remained closed for a third consecutive day due to high winds, making a total of two Gulf of Mexico ports shut, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily report at 1000 local/1600 GMT on Wednesday.

Pajaritos, under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, reopened Wednesday at 0645 local/1245 GMT as wind speeds died down, port officials told Reuters. The port shut Monday at 0440 local/1040 GMT.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state remained closed after closing 0600 local/1200 GMT Monday, with wind speeds reported at 30 km per hour. Port authorities said the port could reopen later in the day.
The largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open for petroleum shipping through the week's high winds and waves.

Pajaritos ships an average 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and Dos Bocas exports 300,000 bpd, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex). Cayo Arcas ships an average of 600,000 bpd.
Tabasco port Frontera was reported shut for the third day amid winds from the north and northwest at 25 km per hour, as other Gulf of Mexico ports reopened at dawn.
Coatzacoalcos, Ensenada, Rosarito, El Mezquital and Salina Cruz ports were closed to smaller boats amid winds between 15 and 35 km per hour.
The report also warned against sailing in the Gulf of Mexico and the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Cold front moving southwest and crossing north Sonora state toward the northern Baja California peninsula, bringing winds of 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 kilometers/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high.

Light rains and clouds along the coasts of Colima, Michoacan and Guerrero with northeast winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high, except in the Gulf of Tehuantepec where northeast winds were reported at 15 to 25 knots (28 to 47 km/17 to 28 miles per hour), with waves from six to 10 feet high.

Cold front lowering temperatures along the shores and drawing north and notheast winds of 10 to 20 knots, with waves at five to seven feet high. Along the northern gulf winds reported at same velocity from the southeast.

Moderate convective activity along the coast of Honduras, bringing light rains and cloudy skies to shores of Quintana Roo and Belize, with winds from east and northeast at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high.
